q: Endangering the safety of persons travelling by railway by a rash or negligent act or omission is punishable under:

options.A: Section 145 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.B: Section 154 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.C: Section 141 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.D: Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989

e: Endangering the safety of persons travelling by railway by a rash or negligent act or omission is punishable under Section 154 of the Railways Act, 1989, with imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both; the graver wilful act is covered by Section 153.

q: Under Section 58 of the Railways Act, 1989, a railway administration may:

options.A: Fix separate fares for female passengers in all classes
options.B: Refuse to carry female passengers travelling alone at night
options.C: Earmark compartments or seats in trains for the exclusive use of female passengers
options.D: Allot a separate quota of wagons for goods booked by women

e: Section 58 of the Railways Act, 1989 empowers a railway administration to earmark compartments or seats in trains for the exclusive use of female passengers.

q: Under Section 65 of the Railways Act, 1989, a Railway Receipt serves as prima facie evidence of:

options.A: The market value of the goods booked under it
options.B: The ownership of the goods by the Railways
options.C: The condition of the goods at the time of delivery
options.D: The weight and the number of packages stated in it, subject to the endorsements made on it

e: Under Section 65 of the Railways Act, 1989 a Railway Receipt is prima facie evidence of the weight and the number of packages stated in it, subject to the endorsements made on it.

q: Where the consignor declares the value of a consignment and pays the prescribed percentage charge on it, the monetary liability of the Railways for loss of, or damage to, the consignment extends up to:

options.A: The value of the consignment declared by the consignor
options.B: The freight charged on the consignment
options.C: A fixed amount for every consignment, irrespective of its value
options.D: Twice the amount of the percentage charge paid

e: Where the consignor declares the value of a consignment and pays the prescribed percentage charge, the monetary liability of the Railways extends up to the value so declared.

q: During a surprise check of a station, cash is found in excess of the balance shown in the station accounts. The excess amount is:

options.A: Retained by the Station Master for meeting petty expenses
options.B: Credited to the account of the Railways and brought into the accounts, the matter being reported for investigation
options.C: Distributed among the booking staff of the station
options.D: Treated as the personal money of the cashier and returned to him

e: Cash found in excess of the balance in station accounts during a surprise check is credited to the Railways and brought into account, and the matter is reported for investigation; it cannot be retained by staff.

q: Delivery of a parcel at the destination station is normally given:

options.A: To any person who identifies the parcel by its description
options.B: Only to the station master of the forwarding station
options.C: On surrender of the Parcel Way Bill by the consignee or his endorsee
options.D: Only after the expiry of the free time allowed for parcels

e: Delivery of a parcel at destination is given on surrender of the Parcel Way Bill by the consignee or his endorsee, the way bill being the document of entitlement to delivery.

q: Articles deposited in the Lost Property Office of the Railways which remain unclaimed for the prescribed period are:

options.A: Handed over free of charge to the person who found them
options.B: Destroyed by the station staff without any record
options.C: Retained in the office indefinitely at no charge
options.D: Disposed of by public auction, the sale proceeds being credited to the Railways if the owner is not traced

e: Articles in the Lost Property Office remaining unclaimed for the prescribed period are disposed of by public auction, and the sale proceeds are credited to the Railways if the owner is not traced.

q: Under the Auto Upgradation Scheme of the Railways:

options.A: A waitlisted or RAC passenger who has opted for the scheme may be allotted accommodation in a higher class, free of charge, at the time of preparation of the chart, if accommodation is available in the higher class
options.B: Every waitlisted passenger is automatically upgraded on payment of the full difference of fare
options.C: A passenger may upgrade his ticket to a higher class at any time after the journey is completed
options.D: Upgradation is allowed only in favour of passengers travelling on Tatkal tickets

e: Under the Auto Upgradation Scheme a waitlisted or RAC passenger who has opted in may be allotted accommodation in a higher class free of charge at charting, if accommodation is available there.

q: A reservation has been made for five passengers under a single PNR. One of them drops out before the journey. The position is that:

options.A: The entire PNR must be cancelled and a fresh booking made for the remaining passengers
options.B: The booking of the individual passenger can be cancelled separately, the reservation of the remaining passengers continuing under the same PNR
options.C: Partial cancellation of a PNR is not permitted under any circumstances
options.D: The fare of the passenger who drops out is forfeited in full in every case

e: Partial cancellation is permitted: the booking of one passenger under a PNR can be cancelled separately, and the reservation of the remaining passengers continues under the same PNR.

q: The charges paid by passengers to the licensed porters (sahayaks) engaged at stations for carrying their luggage:

options.A: Form part of the coaching earnings of the Railways
options.B: Are collected by the Railways and paid to the porters as wages
options.C: Are paid by the passengers directly to the porters and do not form part of the earnings of the Railways
options.D: Form part of the sundry other earnings of the Railways

e: Charges for licensed porters are paid by passengers directly to the porters for the service rendered; they are not collected by the Railways and form no part of railway earnings.

q: The accounts foils of Blank Paper Tickets issued at a station are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office mainly to ensure that:

options.A: The handwriting of the issuing clerk is legible
options.B: The Blank Paper Tickets were issued only to season ticket holders
options.C: The paper used for the tickets was of the prescribed quality
options.D: The fare has been correctly charged for the class and destination and the amount has been duly brought to account in the station accounts

e: Accounts foils of Blank Paper Tickets are checked mainly to ensure the fare was correctly charged for the class and destination and the amount was duly brought to account in the station accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An overcharge of freight detected during the check of accounts in the Traffic Accounts Office is refunded to the party through an overcharge sheet.
2. For an overcharge so detected departmentally, the party is not required to prefer a formal claim before the Railways for its refund.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: An overcharge detected in the Traffic Accounts Office check is refunded through an overcharge sheet, and for such a departmentally detected overcharge the party need not prefer a formal claim, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about luggage carried by a passenger:
1. Luggage up to the free allowance admissible for the class of travel is carried free of charge.
2. Luggage in excess of the free allowance, up to the prescribed marginal allowance, may be booked in the brake van on payment of the luggage charges.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Luggage up to the free allowance for the class is carried free, and luggage in excess of it, up to the prescribed marginal allowance, may be booked in the brake van on payment of luggage charges, so both statements are correct.

q: 'Tonnes terminating' on a railway during a period represent:

options.A: The tonnes of goods unloaded at the stations of that railway, including the traffic received by it from other railways for delivery
options.B: The tonnes of goods booked at the stations of that railway only
options.C: The tonnes of goods handed over by that railway to other railways
options.D: The tonnes of goods transhipped at the break-of-gauge points of that railway

e: Tonnes terminating are the tonnes of goods unloaded at the stations of a railway, including traffic received from other railways for delivery on that railway.

q:
Consider the following statements about Gross Tonne Kilometres:
1. Gross Tonne Kilometres are worked out on the gross trailing load of trains, comprising the tare weight of the vehicles and the weight of their contents.
2. The weight of the locomotive hauling the train is not included in the gross trailing load.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Gross Tonne Kilometres are worked out on the gross trailing load, that is tare weight of vehicles plus weight of contents, and the hauling locomotive's weight is not part of the trailing load, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about allotment of wagons against indents:
1. Wagons are ordinarily allotted to consignors in the order in which their demands (indents) are registered at the station.
2. Such allotment is subject to the priorities laid down in the Preferential Traffic Schedule in force.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Wagons are ordinarily allotted in the order in which indents are registered at the station, subject to the priorities in the Preferential Traffic Schedule in force, so both statements are correct.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation CRIS stands for:

options.A: Central Railway Information Service
options.B: Computerised Reservation and Information System
options.C: Centre for Railway Information Systems
options.D: Centralised Railway Integrated System

e: CRIS stands for Centre for Railway Information Systems, the organisation that develops and maintains the information systems of Indian Railways such as PRS and FOIS.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation IRCA stands for:

options.A: Indian Railway Catering Association
options.B: Indian Railway Conference Association
options.C: Indian Railway Claims Authority
options.D: Indian Railway Commercial Association

e: IRCA stands for Indian Railway Conference Association, the body associated with conference rules, tariffs and through booking arrangements between railways.

q: Besides the booking and rostering of running staff, the data captured in the Crew Management System are used for:

options.A: Compilation of the Station Balance Sheet
options.B: Allotment of wagons against indents
options.C: Preparation of reservation charts
options.D: Watching the hours of duty worked and the rest availed of by the running staff

e: Besides booking and rostering, Crew Management System data are used for watching the hours of duty worked and the rest availed of by running staff, as required under the hours of employment rules.

q: At a parcel office working on the Parcel Management System:

options.A: The parcel is booked through the system, which generates the Parcel Way Bill and computes the charges payable on it
options.B: The system is used only for printing the Station Balance Sheet
options.C: Parcels are booked manually and the system is used only for staff attendance
options.D: The system is used only for the allotment of parcel vans to trains

e: At a Parcel Management System office the parcel is booked through the system, which generates the Parcel Way Bill and computes the charges payable on it.

q: The holder of an earning contract at a station persistently defaults in payment of the licence fee due to the Railways. In such a case, under the terms of the contract:

options.A: The contract continues indefinitely and no action can be taken on the security deposit
options.B: The security deposit held for the contract is liable to be forfeited and the contract is liable to be terminated
options.C: The dues are recovered from the salary of the Station Master
options.D: The dues are written off by the station as a matter of course

e: On persistent default in payment of licence fee, the security deposit held for the earning contract is liable to be forfeited and the contract is liable to be terminated under its terms.

q: The 'Ladies Quota' of reserved accommodation provided in trains is earmarked for allotment to:

options.A: Female railway employees travelling on duty only
options.B: Women members of the families of railway staff only
options.C: Lady passengers travelling alone or with young children, in the trains and classes in which the quota is provided
options.D: Holders of free complimentary passes only

e: The Ladies Quota is earmarked for lady passengers travelling alone or with young children, in the trains and classes in which that quota is provided.

q: The basic document on the basis of which the train performance (operating) statistics of the Railways are compiled is the:

options.A: Station Balance Sheet rendered by the stations
options.B: Passenger classification return rendered by the stations
options.C: Goods abstract prepared in the Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: Combined Train Report rendered for each train

e: The basic document for compiling train performance or operating statistics is the Combined Train Report rendered for each train, which records its running, load and detention particulars.

q: An order of the Railway Claims Tribunal awarding compensation to a claimant is:

options.A: Executable in the same manner as a decree of a civil court
options.B: Only advisory in nature and cannot be enforced
options.C: Enforceable only through a fresh suit in a civil court
options.D: Executable only after it is confirmed by the Railway Board

e: An order of the Railway Claims Tribunal awarding compensation is executable in the same manner as a decree of a civil court, under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act.

q: Under the 'slip coach' arrangement on the Railways:

options.A: A coach is detached from a train and left at the destination station permanently
options.B: Coaches meant for a destination are detached at an intermediate junction and attached to a connecting train, so that the passengers travel through without changing trains
options.C: Passengers are transferred from one train to another at the junction station
options.D: A spare coach is attached to a train only when the train is running late

e: Under the slip coach arrangement, coaches for a destination are detached at an intermediate junction and attached to a connecting train, so passengers travel through without changing trains.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where there is no weighbridge at the forwarding station, a wagonload consignment is weighed at the first available weighbridge en route.
2. The freight on such a consignment is accounted for on the weight so ascertained at the en-route weighbridge.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: 1 only

e: Where there is no weighbridge at the forwarding station, a wagonload consignment is weighed at the first available weighbridge en route and freight is accounted for on that ascertained weight, so both statements are correct.

q: A consignor withdraws his consignment before it is despatched from the forwarding station, after having prepaid the freight on it. The prepaid freight is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railways in full in all cases
options.B: Adjusted against the demurrage of other consignors at the station
options.C: Credited to the sundry earnings of the station
options.D: Refunded to the consignor after deduction of the prescribed cancellation charges

e: If a consignor withdraws his consignment before despatch after prepaying freight, the prepaid freight is refunded to him after deduction of the prescribed cancellation charges.

q: The irregularities noticed by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during his inspection of a station are:

options.A: Communicated to the station for compliance, and their clearance is watched by the Traffic Accounts Office
options.B: Noted by him personally and closed without any report to any office
options.C: Reported only to the statutory audit party after the close of the year
options.D: Adjusted by him on the spot by altering the station accounts himself

e: Irregularities noticed by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during station inspection are communicated to the station for compliance, and their clearance is watched by the Traffic Accounts Office.

q: At goods terminals working on the Terminal Management System of the Freight Operations Information System, the demurrage payable on wagons is:

options.A: Estimated by the goods clerk at the end of the month
options.B: Computed by the system from the placement and removal or release particulars of the wagons recorded in it
options.C: Charged at a flat rate for all wagons irrespective of the period of detention
options.D: Waived in all cases where the terminal is computerised

e: At terminals working on the Terminal Management System of FOIS, demurrage is computed by the system from the placement and removal or release particulars of the wagons recorded in it.

q: Under Section 50 of the Railways Act, 1989:

options.A: A railway administration may refuse to issue a ticket to any person without assigning a reason
options.B: Tickets can be issued only at the station from which the journey commences
options.C: A person desirous of travelling on the railway is entitled, on payment of the fare, to be supplied with a ticket by the railway administration
options.D: A ticket once issued can be transferred freely to any other person

e: Section 50 of the Railways Act, 1989 entitles a person desirous of travelling, on payment of the fare, to be supplied with a ticket by the railway administration.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Demurrage is levied at rates which increase progressively as the period of detention of the wagon beyond the free time increases.
2. Wharfage is the charge levied for the detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for their loading or unloading.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Demurrage rates increase progressively as detention beyond free time increases, so statement 1 is correct; statement 2 is wrong because detention of wagons is demurrage, while wharfage is for goods retained on railway premises beyond free time.

q:
Consider the following statements about the alarm chain apparatus in a train:
1. A passenger may use the alarm chain apparatus in a genuine emergency affecting the safety of the train or of the passengers.
2. Use of the alarm chain apparatus without reasonable and sufficient cause is punishable under Section 141 of the Railways Act, 1989.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A passenger may use the alarm chain apparatus in a genuine emergency affecting safety, and its use without reasonable and sufficient cause is punishable under Section 141, so both statements are correct.

q: The 'Vehicle Guidance' rendered by the guard of a train shows:

options.A: The vehicles composing the train, and forms a basic record for compiling the vehicle-kilometre statistics
options.B: The names of the passengers travelling by the train
options.C: The parcels booked at the stations served by the train
options.D: The earnings collected by the ticket checking staff on the train

e: The Vehicle Guidance rendered by the guard shows the vehicles composing the train and forms a basic record for compiling vehicle-kilometre statistics.

q:
Consider the following statements about hire charges for wagons between railways:
1. Hire charges are payable by a railway for the days for which the wagons of another railway remain on its lines.
2. Such hire charges are settled periodically between the railways on the basis of the interchange records of wagons.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: 1 only
options.D: 2 only

e: Hire charges are payable for the days wagons of another railway remain on a railway's lines, and they are settled periodically between railways on the basis of wagon interchange records, so both statements are correct.

q: In the Freight Operations Information System, the abbreviation FNR stands for:

options.A: Freight Note Register
options.B: Freight Name Record, being the number allotted to a consignment booked through the system
options.C: Final Notice of Removal
options.D: Freight Numbering Register

e: In FOIS, FNR stands for Freight Name Record, the number allotted to a consignment booked through the system, used to identify and track that consignment.

q: The cloak room facility at a railway station is provided for:

options.A: Traders of the locality for storage of their merchandise
options.B: Railway contractors for keeping their tools and materials
options.C: Bonafide passengers holding valid tickets, for depositing their luggage for the prescribed period on payment of the charges
options.D: Members of the public generally, whether they hold a ticket or not

e: The cloak room facility is for bonafide passengers holding valid tickets, who may deposit their luggage for the prescribed period on payment of the charges.

q: The reservation demand and the waitlist position of trains are watched by the Commercial Department mainly in order to:

options.A: Fix the pay and allowances of the reservation staff
options.B: Decide the fares to be charged for unreserved tickets
options.C: Prepare the earnings budget of the railway
options.D: Decide the augmentation of trains with additional coaches and the running of special trains to clear the extra rush

e: Reservation demand and waitlist position are watched by the Commercial Department mainly to decide augmentation of trains with additional coaches and running of special trains to clear extra rush.

q: DEMU trains on Indian Railways are:

options.A: Diesel Electric Multiple Unit trains used mainly for short-distance passenger services, including on non-electrified sections
options.B: Electric Multiple Unit trains run only on suburban sections of metropolitan cities
options.C: Goods trains hauled by two diesel locomotives in multiple operation
options.D: Departmental trains used for the carriage of railway materials

e: DEMU trains are Diesel Electric Multiple Unit trains used mainly for short-distance passenger services, including on non-electrified sections.

q: Garib Rath Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Unreserved trains run for the carriage of seasonal labour traffic
options.B: Fully air-conditioned trains introduced to provide air-conditioned travel at fares lower than those of the ordinary air-conditioned classes
options.C: Trains in which no bedding is provided to the passengers in any class
options.D: Goods trains run for the carriage of foodgrains to deficit areas

e: Garib Rath Express trains are fully air-conditioned trains introduced to provide air-conditioned travel at fares lower than those of the ordinary air-conditioned classes.

q: Parcels are ordinarily carried by the Railways:

options.A: At the railway risk in all cases, the Railways bearing unlimited liability for their loss or damage
options.B: Free of charge when they accompany a travelling passenger
options.C: At the owner's risk, the liability of the Railways being limited unless the sender declares the value and pays the prescribed percentage charge
options.D: Only by goods trains and never by passenger trains

e: Parcels are ordinarily carried at owner's risk; the liability of the Railways is limited unless the sender declares the value and pays the prescribed percentage charge for railway risk.

q: Terminal charges are set apart in the apportionment of goods earnings before the balance is divided by distance, mainly in order to:

options.A: Increase the total earnings of Indian Railways as a whole
options.B: Compensate the railways rendering the terminal services of loading, unloading and documentation, whose work does not vary with the distance carried
options.C: Meet the cost of locomotive haulage over the longest railway
options.D: Provide for the refund of overcharges detected at destination

e: Terminal charges are set apart before dividing the balance of goods earnings by distance, to compensate railways rendering terminal services such as loading, unloading and documentation, whose work does not vary with distance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Traffic density on a section is expressed as Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre of the section.
2. Utilisation of line capacity on a section is expressed as the percentage of the charted capacity of the section actually utilised by trains run.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Traffic density is expressed as Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre, and line capacity utilisation as the percentage of charted capacity actually utilised, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about a freight forwarder:
1. The forwarder's margin lies in collecting small consignments from several consignors and booking them together at wagonload rates in his own name.
2. The Railways pay the forwarder a commission out of the freight collected on such traffic.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A freight forwarder's margin lies in collecting small consignments from several consignors and booking them together at wagonload rates in his own name; the Railways pay him no commission, so statement 1 only is correct.

q: The punctuality percentage of passenger trains on a railway is worked out as:

options.A: The trains departing on time, expressed as a percentage of the trains received from other railways
options.B: The engine kilometres run, expressed as a percentage of the train kilometres run
options.C: The passenger kilometres performed, expressed as a percentage of the seat kilometres offered
options.D: The trains arriving at destination at the right time, expressed as a percentage of the total trains run

e: Punctuality percentage of passenger trains is the trains arriving at destination at the right time expressed as a percentage of the total trains run.

q:
Consider the following statements about passenger kilometres:
1. Passenger kilometres include the journeys performed on season tickets, estimated on the prescribed standard basis.
2. Passenger kilometres aggregate the journeys of both suburban and non-suburban passengers.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Passenger kilometres include season ticket journeys estimated on the prescribed standard basis and aggregate both suburban and non-suburban passengers, so both statements are correct.

q: The claims prevention work on a zonal railway is directed mainly towards:

options.A: Deciding the compensation claims filed before the Railway Claims Tribunal
options.B: Reducing the incidence of claims by supervising loading, unloading, packing, marking and documentation of consignments and by inspecting goods sheds and parcel offices
options.C: Recovering the licence fees due under earning contracts at stations
options.D: Compiling the commodity statistics of the railway

e: Claims prevention work aims at reducing the incidence of claims by supervising loading, unloading, packing, marking and documentation and by inspecting goods sheds and parcel offices.

q: In container traffic operated by CONCOR, the commercial relationship is that:

options.A: The customer pays the container operator for the door-to-door service, and the operator in turn pays haulage charges to the Railways for movement over the railway network
options.B: The customer pays freight to the Railways and the Railways pay a commission to the operator out of it
options.C: The Railways collect the customer's charges and hand over the entire amount to the operator
options.D: No charges are payable by anyone, container movement being a free service

e: In CONCOR container traffic the customer pays the operator for the door-to-door service, and the operator in turn pays haulage charges to the Railways for movement over the railway network.

q: A platform ticket issued to a visitor at a station authorises the holder only to:

options.A: Travel in the unreserved coach of any train leaving the station
options.B: Occupy a seat in the waiting room for twenty-four hours
options.C: Book luggage at the parcel office at concessional rates
options.D: Enter the station platform for the period of its validity, and does not authorise him to travel by any train

e: A platform ticket authorises the holder only to enter the station platform for the period of its validity; it does not authorise travel by any train.

q:
Consider the following statements about through traffic earnings:
1. The full fare or freight on through traffic is collected at the booking point by the booking railway.
2. The booking railway retains only its own share of that amount, the shares of the other railways concerned being passed to them through the apportionment of earnings.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: On through traffic the full fare or freight is collected by the booking railway, which retains only its own share and passes the other railways' shares through apportionment, so both statements are correct.

q: The fare of a Monthly Season Ticket is fixed on the basis that it is:

options.A: Equal to the fare for thirty single journeys at full rates
options.B: A highly concessional multiple-journey fare, far below the aggregate of the single-journey fares for the journeys it permits during the month
options.C: Equal to the fare of a single return journey in the same class
options.D: Charged at the Tatkal premium rates for the section

e: A Monthly Season Ticket fare is a highly concessional multiple-journey fare, far below the aggregate of single-journey fares for the journeys it permits during the month.

q: A concession in passenger fares can be granted at a station only:

options.A: At the discretion of the booking clerk on duty
options.B: At the discretion of the Station Master in deserving cases
options.C: On the verbal orders of the Travelling Inspector of Accounts
options.D: Where it is admissible under the concession orders in force, issued by the competent authority, and on production of the prescribed certificate or document where one is required

e: A fare concession can be granted at a station only where it is admissible under the concession orders in force issued by the competent authority, and on production of the prescribed certificate or document where required.

q: A surprise check of the cash and accounts of a station may be conducted by:

options.A: Authorised officers and inspectors of the Accounts and Commercial departments, and not by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts alone
options.B: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts alone, and by no other official
options.C: The licensed porters engaged at the station
options.D: The Railway Protection Force alone

e: A surprise check of station cash and accounts may be conducted by authorised officers and inspectors of the Accounts and Commercial departments, not by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts alone.

q:
Consider the following statements about wagon kilometres:
1. Total wagon kilometres of a railway are the sum of its loaded wagon kilometres and empty wagon kilometres.
2. A rising proportion of empty wagon kilometres generally signals a directional imbalance of traffic, with wagons returning empty for want of return loading.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Total wagon kilometres are the sum of loaded and empty wagon kilometres, and a rising proportion of empty kilometres generally signals directional imbalance of traffic, so both statements are correct.

q: Where the refund of fare on a ticket is not automatic, the passenger can claim it by filing a Ticket Deposit Receipt:

options.A: At any time, without any time limit
options.B: Within the time limits prescribed in the refund rules for the purpose
options.C: Only after one year from the date of journey
options.D: Only through a civil court

e: Where fare refund is not automatic, the passenger claims it by filing a Ticket Deposit Receipt within the time limits prescribed in the refund rules.

q: For container trains run over the railway network, the commercial risk of filling the containers and finding the traffic rests with:

options.A: The Traffic Accounts Office of the zonal railway
options.B: The station staff of the gateway port station
options.C: The Railway Board's Statistics Directorate
options.D: The container train operator, the Railways rendering the haulage service for the charges recovered from the operator

e: For container trains the commercial risk of filling the containers and finding the traffic rests with the container train operator; the Railways only render haulage for the charges recovered from the operator.

q: Unclaimed perishable consignments at a station are disposed of promptly, without waiting for the full period prescribed for ordinary unclaimed goods, because:

options.A: Delay would cause deterioration and loss of value of the goods, to the detriment of all concerned
options.B: Perishable goods are exempt from all railway dues
options.C: The station staff are entitled to consume such goods
options.D: No record of perishable consignments is maintained at stations

e: Unclaimed perishable consignments are disposed of promptly, without waiting the full period for ordinary goods, because delay would cause deterioration and loss of value to the detriment of all concerned.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A party claiming refund of an overcharge of freight must prefer his claim to the railway administration within the period prescribed under the Railways Act.
2. An overcharge detected departmentally during the check of accounts in the Traffic Accounts Office is refunded through an overcharge sheet without requiring the party to prefer a formal claim.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A party's own overcharge claim must be preferred within the period prescribed under the Railways Act, while a departmentally detected overcharge is refunded through an overcharge sheet without a formal claim, so both statements are correct.

q: The Conference Rules and the Goods Tariff issued under the authority of the Indian Railway Conference Association primarily govern:

options.A: The pay and allowances of goods shed staff
options.B: The rating, classification and conditions of carriage of goods traffic, including through booking between railways
options.C: The compilation of the Station Balance Sheet
options.D: The allotment of quarters to commercial staff

e: The Conference Rules and Goods Tariff issued under IRCA authority govern the rating, classification and conditions of carriage of goods traffic, including through booking between railways.

q: For the purposes of railway accident statistics, train accidents are distinguished and reported separately from:

options.A: Passenger train accidents only
options.B: Accidents occurring in yards and sidings, equipment failures and other incidents which are not train accidents
options.C: Accidents in which passengers are injured
options.D: Accidents enquired into by the Commissioner of Railway Safety

e: For accident statistics, train accidents are distinguished and reported separately from accidents in yards and sidings, equipment failures and other incidents which are not train accidents.

q: Delivery of a 'to-pay' consignment without collection of the freight due is liable to be detected in the Traffic Accounts Office by:

options.A: Tallying the delivery records and gate passes of the destination station with the invoices and inward returns received for the traffic
options.B: Counting the wagons standing in the goods shed
options.C: Verifying the handwriting of the delivery clerk
options.D: Comparing the earnings of the station with those of the previous year only

e: Delivery of a to-pay consignment without collecting freight is detected by tallying the delivery records and gate passes of the destination station with the invoices and inward returns for the traffic.

q:
Consider the following statements about the excess charge realised from a person travelling without a proper ticket:
1. The excess charge is levied in addition to the ordinary fare due for the distance travelled.
2. The excess charge is in the nature of a deterrent against ticketless travel, and is distinct from the fare itself.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The excess charge is levied in addition to the ordinary fare for the distance travelled and is in the nature of a deterrent against ticketless travel, distinct from the fare itself, so both statements are correct.

q: At the close of a shift, the cash remitted by a booking office working on the Unreserved Ticketing System falls short of the amount shown in the system-generated shift summary. The shortage is:

options.A: Written off by the booking clerk at the close of the shift
options.B: Debited to the station and shown as recoverable from the staff responsible, in the station accounts
options.C: Adjusted against the earnings of the reservation office
options.D: Borne by the passengers who purchased tickets in that shift

e: A UTS shift shortage, where cash remitted falls short of the system shift summary, is debited to the station and shown as recoverable from the staff responsible in the station accounts.

q: A military unit moves by a special train booked on military credit notes. Until the charges are billed on and recovered from the Defence authorities, the amount is:

options.A: Treated as free traffic and excluded from the accounts altogether
options.B: Recovered in cash from the individual soldiers travelling in the train
options.C: Written off as a social service obligation of the Railways
options.D: Watched as a credit item recoverable from the department concerned, through the traffic accounts

e: For a military special train booked on military credit notes, the charges are watched as a credit item recoverable from the Defence authorities through the traffic accounts until billed and recovered.

q: A passenger is found travelling without a ticket and is unable to establish the station from which he boarded the train. The fare and excess charge are realised from him:

options.A: From the station from which the train started, as the boarding point is not established
options.B: Only from the station at which the ticket checking staff boarded the train
options.C: Only up to the next station at which the train stops
options.D: At a flat amount, irrespective of the distance involved

e: Where a ticketless passenger cannot establish his boarding station, fare and excess charge are realised from the station from which the train started, as the boarding point is not established.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The ten-day statement of approximate earnings is compiled on the originating basis because apportionment of through earnings takes time and the figures are required quickly.
2. The earnings finally brought to account for the month are on the apportioned basis, after internal check.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The ten-day approximate earnings statement is on the originating basis because apportionment takes time and figures are needed quickly, while final monthly earnings are on the apportioned basis after internal check, so both statements are correct.

q: The follow-up of outstandings shown in the Accounts Office Balance Sheet is exercised by the Traffic Accounts Office mainly by:

options.A: Closing all items outstanding for more than a month without recovery
options.B: Pursuing the items, age-wise and station-wise, with the stations and the divisional authorities till they are cleared or adjusted with proper sanction
options.C: Transferring all outstandings to the Railway Board at the end of the month
options.D: Recovering the amounts from the passengers and merchants of the station directly

e: Follow-up of Accounts Office Balance Sheet outstandings is done by pursuing items age-wise and station-wise with stations and divisional authorities till they are cleared or adjusted with proper sanction.

q: A Railway Receipt endorsed in favour of a bank enables the bank to:

options.A: Run trains over the railway network against the consignment
options.B: Fix the freight rates for the consignor's future traffic
options.C: Waive the demurrage accrued on the consignment
options.D: Hold the document of title to the goods as security for the advance made to the trader, and take delivery on surrender of the receipt

e: A Railway Receipt endorsed in favour of a bank lets the bank hold the document of title to the goods as security for its advance to the trader and take delivery on surrender of the receipt.

q: Luggage deposited in the cloak room of a station which is not claimed within the maximum period allowed for its deposit is:

options.A: Treated thereafter as unclaimed property and dealt with under the rules for unclaimed articles, after due notice
options.B: Retained in the cloak room indefinitely without any charge
options.C: Handed over free of charge to the cloak room attendant
options.D: Destroyed by the station staff without any record

e: Cloak room luggage not claimed within the maximum period allowed is treated thereafter as unclaimed property and dealt with under the rules for unclaimed articles, after due notice.

q:
Consider the following statements about fares under the flexi fare system:
1. The flexi increase, as the proportion of accommodation sold rises, applies to the base fare of the ticket.
2. Charges other than the base fare, such as the reservation charge and the superfast charge, are levied separately as applicable and are not themselves flexed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under flexi fare, the increase as the proportion of accommodation sold rises applies to the base fare, while reservation charge, superfast charge and other charges are levied separately and are not flexed, so both statements are correct.

q: The seat kilometres offered by a railway remain unchanged in a period, but its passenger kilometres rise. The correct inference is that:

options.A: The capacity provided by the railway has increased
options.B: The occupation (load factor) of the coaching services has improved, the same capacity being better utilised
options.C: The number of trains run has necessarily increased
options.D: The earnings of the railway have necessarily fallen

e: If seat kilometres offered are unchanged but passenger kilometres rise, the occupation or load factor of coaching services has improved, the same capacity being better utilised.

q: Charges for Government traffic booked on credit notes are debited under Traffic Suspense at a station. Their clearance is effected by:

options.A: Raising bills on the departments concerned and recovering the amounts from them
options.B: Writing off the debits at the close of the financial year in all cases
options.C: Recovering the amounts from the station staff in equal shares
options.D: Adjusting the debits against the sundry earnings of the station

e: Government traffic debited under Traffic Suspense on credit notes is cleared by raising bills on the departments concerned and recovering the amounts from them.

q: Over a period, a zonal railway consistently receives more loaded wagons at interchange points from other railways than it hands over to them. Other things remaining equal, the effect is that:

options.A: Its wagon turn-round necessarily becomes nil
options.B: Its earnings are transferred in full to the other railways
options.C: Its Specific Fuel Consumption necessarily falls to zero
options.D: Its wagon holding on line increases, the surplus wagons accumulating on its system

e: If a railway consistently receives more loaded wagons at interchange than it hands over, its wagon holding on line increases, the surplus wagons accumulating on its system, other things remaining equal.

q:
Consider the following statements about the monthly evaluation of earnings:
1. The evaluation compares the earnings actually brought to account with the budget proportions for the month.
2. A persistent shortfall against the budget proportions calls for investigation into its causes, which may include a fall in traffic or leakage of revenue.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Monthly evaluation compares earnings actually brought to account with the budget proportions for the month, and a persistent shortfall calls for investigation into causes such as fall in traffic or leakage, so both statements are correct.

q: Domestic container traffic on Indian Railways is traffic which:

options.A: Moves only between two gateway ports by sea
options.B: Moves between inland container depots and terminals within the country, as distinct from export-import traffic moving between ports and inland depots
options.C: Is carried free of haulage charges in all cases
options.D: Is booked only on parcel way bills

e: Domestic container traffic moves between inland container depots and terminals within the country, as distinct from export-import traffic moving between ports and inland depots.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Claims for compensation for loss of, damage to or non-delivery of goods are dealt with by the claims organisation of the Commercial Department of the railway.
2. Such claims are settled and paid by the Traffic Accounts Office in the course of its internal check of station accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Goods compensation claims are dealt with by the claims organisation of the Commercial Department; they are not settled and paid by the Traffic Accounts Office in its internal check, so statement 1 only is correct.

q: Monthly Statistical Statement 7-B of Indian Railways relates to:

options.A: Fuel and power statistics
options.B: Rolling stock (locomotive) performance
options.C: Commodity statistics of goods traffic
options.D: Goods Revenue Statistics (on originating basis)

e: Monthly Statistical Statement 7-B relates to Goods Revenue Statistics on the originating basis, showing revenue from goods traffic originating on the railway.

q:
Consider the following statements about a Monthly Season Ticket:
1. The holder is issued a photo identity card along with the season ticket and is required to carry it during the journey.
2. The season ticket entitles the holder to travel only in the unreserved accommodation of the class and over the section for which it is issued.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A Monthly Season Ticket holder is issued a photo identity card to carry during the journey, and the ticket entitles travel only in unreserved accommodation of the class and section for which it is issued, so both statements are correct.

q: Settlements between zonal railways for traffic interchanged with each other are effected:

options.A: In cash, by the Station Masters of the junction stations every day
options.B: Through the apportionment and transfer adjustments in the accounts of the railways concerned, on the basis of the interchange and invoice abstracts exchanged between them
options.C: Only at the close of the financial year, by the Railway Board in cash
options.D: By the consignors and passengers travelling over both the railways

e: Settlements between zonal railways for interchanged traffic are effected through apportionment and transfer adjustments in their accounts, on the basis of the interchange and invoice abstracts exchanged between them.

q: A 'to-pay' consignment is delivered at the destination station, but through oversight the freight due on it is not collected from the consignee. Until the amount is recovered, it is shown in the station accounts as:

options.A: A goods outstanding recoverable at the station
options.B: A sundry earning of the station
options.C: A refund payable to the consignor
options.D: Cash-in-transit of the forwarding station

e: A to-pay consignment delivered without collecting the freight due leaves the amount shown in the station accounts as a goods outstanding recoverable at the station until it is recovered.

q: Where the output of shunting work cannot be expressed in tonne kilometres, the performance and consumption indices for shunting are worked out with reference to:

options.A: The number of passengers carried in the yard
options.B: The route kilometres of the yard
options.C: The number of wagons owned by the railway
options.D: The shunting engine hours performed

e: Where shunting output cannot be expressed in tonne kilometres, performance and consumption indices for shunting are worked out with reference to the shunting engine hours performed.

q: Freight on traffic carried on Railway Material Consignment notes is accounted for:

options.A: In cash, collected from the consignee at the destination station
options.B: As commercial goods earnings of the railway, like ordinary public traffic
options.C: By transfer adjustment in the books, and is not treated as part of the commercial traffic earnings
options.D: By deduction from the sundry earnings of the forwarding station

e: Freight on Railway Material Consignment notes is accounted for by transfer adjustment in the books and is not treated as part of the commercial traffic earnings of the railway.

q: The Cash Witness in the traffic Cash Office is associated with:

options.A: The checking of collected tickets rendered by stations
options.B: Witnessing the counting and acknowledgement of the cash remitted by stations, the acknowledgement foil being returned to the station
options.C: The compilation of the passenger classification returns
options.D: The sanction of refunds of fares at stations

e: The Cash Witness in the traffic Cash Office witnesses the counting and acknowledgement of cash remitted by stations, the acknowledgement foil being returned to the station.

q: Goods and Services Tax on passenger fares on Indian Railways is levied:

options.A: On the fares of the air-conditioned classes of travel, the fares of the non-air-conditioned classes being outside its levy
options.B: Uniformly on the fares of all classes, including the unreserved second class
options.C: Only on the reservation charge, and not on the fare
options.D: Only on tickets booked under the Tatkal scheme

e: GST on passenger fares is levied on the fares of the air-conditioned classes of travel; fares of the non-air-conditioned classes are outside its levy.

q: The Pooled Quota of reserved accommodation in a train is a quota which is:

options.A: Reserved exclusively for the holders of season tickets
options.B: Allotted only at the originating station of the train
options.C: Meant only for defence personnel travelling on warrants
options.D: Pooled for allotment to passengers boarding at a group of intermediate stations which share that common quota

e: The Pooled Quota is pooled for allotment to passengers boarding at a group of intermediate stations which share that common quota, instead of each station having a separate quota.

q: A magisterial ticket-checking drive on the Railways is distinguished by the fact that:

options.A: It is conducted only inside the reservation offices
options.B: No excess charge is realised from any passenger during the drive
options.C: A Railway Magistrate accompanies the checking squad, so that offenders can be prosecuted and dealt with on the spot
options.D: It is confined to the checking of season tickets alone

e: A magisterial ticket-checking drive is distinguished by a Railway Magistrate accompanying the checking squad, so offenders can be prosecuted and dealt with on the spot.

q: The detailed rules and instructions governing the commercial working of stations, such as booking of passengers, parcels and goods, fares and refunds, are contained in the:

options.A: Accounts Code, Volume II
options.B: Indian Railway Commercial Manual
options.C: Indian Railway Stores Code
options.D: Indian Railway Works Manual

e: The detailed rules for commercial working of stations, covering booking of passengers, parcels and goods, fares and refunds, are contained in the Indian Railway Commercial Manual.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A clerkage charge is deducted where an unused ticket is surrendered by a passenger for refund of the fare.
2. A cancellation charge is deducted where a reserved ticket is cancelled by a passenger.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A clerkage charge is deducted when an unused ticket is surrendered for refund, and a cancellation charge is deducted when a reserved ticket is cancelled, so both statements are correct.

q: The Commercial Department of a zonal railway, which is responsible for traffic earnings, reservation, catering and other commercial activities, is headed by the:

options.A: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer
options.B: Principal Chief Commercial Manager
options.C: Principal Chief Operations Manager
options.D: Chief Traffic Manager

e: The Commercial Department of a zonal railway, responsible for traffic earnings, reservation, catering and other commercial activities, is headed by the Principal Chief Commercial Manager.

q: A passenger holding a confirmed Sleeper class reserved ticket approaches a computerised reservation counter before the journey and asks for accommodation in AC 3-Tier in the same train, berths being available. The correct position is that:

options.A: His accommodation can be upgraded to the higher class on payment of the difference of fare, subject to availability
options.B: He must cancel the ticket, bear the cancellation charges and make a fresh booking
options.C: Upgradation is possible only free of charge, under the Auto Upgradation Scheme at the time of charting
options.D: Upgradation of a confirmed ticket to a higher class is never permitted

e: A confirmed ticket holder can be upgraded to a higher class in the same train before the journey on payment of the difference of fare, subject to availability of accommodation.

q: Endangering the safety of persons travelling by railway by a wilful act or omission is punishable under:

options.A: Section 153 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.B: Section 154 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.C: Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.D: Section 156 of the Railways Act, 1989

e: Section 153 of the Railways Act, 1989 punishes endangering the safety of persons travelling by railway by a wilful act or omission - an unlawful act or wilful omission or neglect - with imprisonment up to five years; Section 154 covers the lesser rash or negligent act.

q:
Consider the following statements about engine hours:
1. Engine hours are classified according to the employment of the engine, such as train engine hours, shunting hours and light or assisting engine hours.
2. Indices based on engine hours are used for services such as shunting, whose output cannot conveniently be expressed in tonne kilometres.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Engine hours are classified by employment of the engine, such as train, shunting and light or assisting hours, and engine-hour indices are used for services like shunting whose output cannot conveniently be expressed in tonne kilometres, so both statements are correct.

q: The Daily Traffic Cash Statement rendered by a station shows, in respect of each day:

options.A: The traffic cash collections of the day and the manner of their remittance or disposal
options.B: Only the number of tickets sold during the day
options.C: The attendance of the booking staff of the station
options.D: The goods delivered at the station during the day

e: The Daily Traffic Cash Statement shows, for each day, the traffic cash collections of the station and the manner of their remittance or disposal.

q: A passenger travelling in AC First Class wishes to carry his dog with him in the compartment itself. The correct position is that:

options.A: A dog can in no case be carried in a passenger compartment
options.B: The dog is carried free of charge in the compartment
options.C: The dog can be carried only in the brake van, whatever the class of travel
options.D: The dog may be carried in the AC First Class compartment on payment of the prescribed charges, subject to the dog being removed to the brake van if a co-passenger objects

e: A dog may be carried in an AC First Class compartment on payment of the prescribed charges, subject to the dog being removed to the brake van if a co-passenger objects.

q: Claims for refund of fares which cannot be granted across the counter at a station are dealt with, after the prescribed verification, by:

options.A: The Traffic Accounts Office of the zonal railway
options.B: The Railway Claims Tribunal, in the first instance in every case
options.C: The refund office of the Commercial Department of the zonal railway, working under the Chief Commercial Manager (Refunds)
options.D: The Railway Board directly

e: Fare refund claims that cannot be granted across the counter are dealt with, after prescribed verification, by the refund office of the Commercial Department working under the Chief Commercial Manager (Refunds).

q:
Consider the following statements about goods in a defective condition:
1. Where goods are in a defective condition or are defectively packed and that fact is recorded in the Forwarding Note and on the Railway Receipt, Section 98 of the Railways Act, 1989 restricts the liability of the Railways for loss or damage arising from that defective condition.
2. The recording of the defective condition on the Railway Receipt has no effect at all on the liability of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Where defective condition or defective packing is recorded in the Forwarding Note and on the Railway Receipt, Section 98 of the Railways Act, 1989 restricts railway liability for loss or damage arising from that condition, so statement 1 only is correct.

q: The printed card tickets stocked and sold at stations are commonly known as:

options.A: Edmondson tickets
options.B: Blank paper tickets
options.C: Excess fare tickets
options.D: Season tickets

e: The printed card tickets stocked and sold at stations are commonly known as Edmondson tickets, after the card ticket system of that name.

q: A motorist who crosses an unmanned level crossing negligently, without stopping and looking out for an approaching train, commits an offence punishable under:

options.A: Section 147 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.B: Section 161 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.C: Section 144 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.D: Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989

e: A motorist who crosses an unmanned level crossing negligently without stopping and looking out for an approaching train commits an offence punishable under Section 161 of the Railways Act, 1989.

q:
Consider the following statements about the social service obligations of the Railways:
1. The carriage of certain essential commodities at freight rates below the cost of working is one of the social service obligations borne by the Railways.
2. The cost of such obligations is borne by the Railways themselves, being broadly cross-subsidised from their other earnings, and is not recovered from the passengers or consignors concerned.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Carriage of essential commodities below the cost of working is a social service obligation of the Railways, whose cost is borne by the Railways and broadly cross-subsidised from other earnings, so both statements are correct.

q: In the assessment of the punctuality of passenger trains, a train is said to be 'not losing time' when it:

options.A: Departs from its originating station at the right time
options.B: Reaches its destination without losing time en route as compared with its booked timings
options.C: Gains time en route and arrives before its scheduled time
options.D: Runs through all intermediate stations without halting

e: In punctuality assessment a train is said to be not losing time when it reaches its destination without losing time en route as compared with its booked timings.

q: A consignment is delivered at the destination station with its packages torn and the contents damaged. To support his compensation claim, the consignee should obtain from the station, at the time of delivery:

options.A: A damage certificate recording the extent of the damage to the consignment
options.B: A shortage certificate for the consignment
options.C: An error sheet issued by the Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: An overcharge sheet for refund of the freight

e: For a consignment delivered with packages torn and contents damaged, the consignee should obtain a damage certificate from the station at the time of delivery, recording the extent of damage, to support his compensation claim.
